resources.name: query-safety
resources.title: Snowflake Query Safety
resources.description: Required safety boundaries and bounded-result practices for snow-kit queries.
resources.summary: Use these boundaries for every Snowflake query. Server-side validation remains authoritative if this resource is not read.

sections.heading: Before querying
items: Use approved analytics context when available, then inspect relevant metadata with catalog tools. Never invent table or column names.
If authoritative context is unavailable, say so. Do not substitute broad INFORMATION_SCHEMA exploration for missing business context.
Prefer fully qualified object names and select only the columns needed.

sections.heading: Bound the work
items: Add an explicit SQL LIMIT when sampling. query_execute max_rows only caps rows returned to the client; it does not add LIMIT or reduce warehouse scanning.
Use catalog_describe_table before catalog_preview_table. Preview can expose sensitive row values, so request the smallest useful limit.
Treat warnings and truncated=true as part of the result, not as successful completeness.

sections.heading: Mutation boundary
items: query_execute accepts only read-safe statements, although USE changes the shared Snowflake session context.
Write tools are hidden by default and still require explicit confirmation, justification, SQL policy validation, and a live-grant preflight when enabled.

resources.name: analytics-workflow
resources.title: Context-Grounded Analytics Workflow
resources.description: A metadata-first workflow for evidence-backed Snowflake analysis.
resources.summary: Separate authoritative business meaning, observed Snowflake metadata, query results, and inference so the final answer is auditable.

sections.heading: Workflow
items: Read snow-kit://context/sources/status. If no authoritative source is available, disclose that limitation before analytical work.
Ground metric definitions, cohorts, filters, and time semantics in approved context when available.
Inspect the smallest relevant catalog scope, describe candidate tables, and only then compose bounded SQL.
Start with counts or narrow samples, validate assumptions against returned metadata, and expand only when justified.

sections.heading: Report
items: Label business definitions as context evidence, schemas and grants as observed metadata, returned values as query evidence, and synthesis as inference.
Carry forward source unavailability, truncation, permission, and freshness warnings.
Do not claim that an empty or failed lookup proves the underlying data does not exist.

resources.name: permissions-and-recovery
resources.title: Permissions and Recovery
resources.description: How to interpret access evidence and recover from snow-kit failures safely.
resources.summary: Treat live Snowflake behavior as decisive. Local permission-spec context is explanatory and must never be presented as proof of effective access.

sections.heading: Permission evidence
items: Use catalog_check_write_access for a bounded preflight. A positive preflight does not guarantee execution; Snowflake remains authoritative.
If local permission-spec context is unavailable or unrecognized, keep the result unknown and use live grants or the attempted operation for decisive evidence.
Never enable write access merely to diagnose a read or metadata failure.

sections.heading: Recovery
items: Auth errors require sign-in or SSO recovery; do not retry them as transient failures.
Permission errors require a role, grant, or object-scope correction. Do not broaden discovery to work around denied access.
Validation errors require corrected input or SQL. Timeout means the outcome may be unknown; reduce scope before retrying.
Retry transient network failures at most once and only when the operation is safe to repeat. query_execute containing USE is not declared idempotent.
